title: josuke.json
description: Deployment ledger for a diamond proxy and its facets, per chain.

gitCommit.description: Full git commit the facet sources were built from.

sourceId.description: A concrete facet source with no globs: "<path>:<ContractName>" for a Solidity contract, or "<path>.evm" for an evm-assembler source facet built via the Makefile that governs its directory.

facetSrc.description: Source patterns whose contracts are facets of this proxy. Each entry is a glob over .sol files ("src/facets/*.sol"), a single "<path>:<ContractName>", or an evm-assembler source file ("<path>.evm").

deployments.description: Keyed by EVM chain id in decimal ("314" = Filecoin mainnet).

current.description: The facet set currently installed on the proxy.

proposed.description: A pending upgrade awaiting execution. Merged into "current" by `josuke accept` once the migration is confirmed on chain.

migration.description: The migration script the proxy delegatecalls to apply this upgrade. Present on "proposed"; retained on "current" once accepted. Its bytecode is fully determined by this deploymentState, so only the address is recorded.

selectors.description: The generated delegate serving ERC-8167 `selectors()`: it returns every selector this deploymentState installs. Synthesized by `josuke deploy` when no facet implements `selectors()`; its bytecode is fully determined by the facet set, so only the address is recorded.

address.description: Where this facet is deployed. Recorded for facets (re)deployed by the upgrade script.

codehash.description: keccak-256 of the deployed runtime bytecode, i.e. what EXTCODEHASH returns for `address`.

initcodeHash.description: keccak-256 of the full creation bytecode: the compiled init bytecode concatenated with the ABI-encoded constructorArgs. Reproducible from gitCommit + constructorArgs, and what the verifier recomputes from source.

constructorArgs.description: Constructor arguments keyed by parameter name. Values are JSON encodings of the ABI types: address and bytesN as 0x hex strings, arrays as arrays, integers as JSON number literals. Integer values are fed to eth_abi.encode, which requires a Python int, so they are kept as bare numbers rather than strings; parse this file with an integer-preserving JSON reader (Python's json is fine — JSON.parse and jq lose precision above 2^53).

from.description: Deployer address, supplied as msg.sender when the verifier re-simulates the constructor. Record it when an immutable is derived from the deployer; omit it otherwise.
